{
  "verdict": "PASS",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "WARNING",
      "file": "apps/web/src/presentation/meeting-room/presentation/chat/chat-panel.tsx",
      "line": 47,
      "claim": "Chat messages that arrive while the pane is hidden never scroll the log, so reopening the chat shows a stale scroll position even though the reader never scrolled up, violating the file's own stick-to-end contract on the most common path (message arrives while panel closed, then user opens chat).",
      "evidence": "useEffect(() => { const body = bodyRef.current; if (body !== null && atEnd.current && count > 0) body.scrollTop = body.scrollHeight; }, [count]); — the effect only runs when `count` changes. While the pane is hidden (RoomSheetPane sets hidden={!shown}; the sheet is also invisible when closed) scrollHeight is 0, so the write is a no-op; when the pane becomes visible no effect re-runs (count unchanged), and `atEnd.current` stays true so no scroll event fires either.",
      "suggested_fix": "Re-run the stick-to-end scroll when the pane becomes visible: add `shown`/`active` to the effect deps (or use a ResizeObserver on the body), scrolling to the end when atEnd.current is true and the pane goes from hidden to shown."
    },
    {
      "severity": "WARNING",
      "file": "packages/realtime/src/realtime-room/infrastructure/livekit/text-streams.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "claim": "Received chat messages are appended in stream-completion order, not send order, so the 'oldest first' log can display messages out of order; with the 10s READ_TIMEOUT a stalled earlier message appends after later ones.",
      "evidence": "const receiveChat = async (session, reader, from) => { const text = await readText(reader, \"chat\", MAX_CHAT_STREAM_BYTES); ... append(message); } — each handler appends only after readText resolves, so two concurrent streams append in completion order (e.g. a large or slow first message lands after a later small one).",
      "suggested_fix": "Insert received messages ordered by reader.info.timestamp (insertion sort into `chat`, or buffer per arrival with a small ordering window) instead of blind append, so the log and the use-chat index bookkeeping match chronological order."
    },
    {
      "severity": "WARNING",
      "file": "apps/web/src/presentation/meeting-room/presentation/room-sheet/use-room-sheet.ts",
      "line": 17,
      "claim": "Focus is not returned to the opening control when the sheet is closed via the scrim, because the guard no-ops once the click has blurred focus out of the sheet; in Chromium focus ends up on body and keyboard users restart from the top of the document (WCAG 2.4.3).",
      "evidence": "function returnFocusTo(pane: RoomPaneId): void { const sheet = document.getElementById(ROOM_SHEET_ID); if (sheet === null || !sheet.contains(document.activeElement)) return; ... } — RoomSheetScrim's onClick path runs after mousedown on a non-focusable div has already moved activeElement to body, so the guard returns early.",
      "suggested_fix": "Capture document.activeElement when toggle() opens the sheet and unconditionally restore focus to it (or to paneControlId(pane)) in close(), rather than conditioning on focus still being inside the sheet."
    },
    {
      "severity": "SUGGESTION",
      "file": "apps/web/src/presentation/meeting-room/presentation/chat/chat-composer.tsx",
      "line": 82,
      "claim": "Text typed while a send is in flight is silently destroyed: the textarea stays editable during `sending`, but the success path unconditionally clears it.",
      "evidence": "setSending(true); void onSend(text, sentChoice).then((result) => { ... if (result.ok) { setText(\"\"); ... } — a user who keeps typing between pressing Send and the promise resolving loses everything they added.",
      "suggested_fix": "Only clear when the field is unchanged since the send (compare to the sent text), or make the textarea readOnly while sending."
    },
    {
      "severity": "SUGGESTION",
      "file": "packages/application/src/meeting/realtime-room.ts",
      "line": 38,
      "claim": "The session chat array grows without bound; the 2000-code-point limit bounds only a single message, so a remote participant (or script) can flood the topic and grow every receiving client's memory and rendered log without limit.",
      "evidence": "readonly chat: readonly ChatMessage[]; — 'Append-only while connected' with no cap, and text-streams.ts appends every accepted stream (append = () => { chat = [...chat, message]; host.refresh(); }).",
      "suggested_fix": "Cap retained chat entries (count or total bytes) with drop-oldest, and note the truncation in the UI, so a flood cannot exhaust memory on all participants."
    },
    {
      "severity": "SUGGESTION",
      "file": "packages/realtime/src/realtime-room/domain/chat-codec.ts",
      "line": 53,
      "claim": "The private/everyone label shown to recipients is taken solely from a sender-supplied attribute while actual delivery is controlled by destinationIdentities, so a non-conforming or modified client can broadcast a message to everyone that every recipient renders as 'Private to you' — misrepresenting a public message as 1:1.",
      "evidence": "export function receivedAudience(attributes, localIdentity) { return attributes?.[AUDIENCE_ATTRIBUTE] === PRIVATE ? privateTo(localIdentity) : EVERYONE; } — nothing ties the 'private' attribute to the presence of a single destination identity.",
      "suggested_fix": "Document and verify (server-side rule or client-side cross-check where the transport exposes destinations) that a 'private'-attributed stream always carries exactly one destination identity; otherwise word received private copy without implying exclusivity."
    }
  ]
}
